A_target.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a [[Definition:Hyperbolic Triangle|triangle]] in the [[Definition:Hyperbolic Plane|hyperbolic plane]] of curvature $-1$.
Then:
:$\cosh c = \cosh a \cosh b - \sinh a \sinh b \cos C$

B_source.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a [[Definition:Spherical Triangle|spherical triangle]] on the unit sphere.
Then:
:$\cos c = \cos a \cos b + \sin a \sin b \cos C$

derived.cos c = cos a cos b + sin a sin b cos C: cosh c = cosh a cosh b - sinh a sinh b cos C

object_map.reformulation: Replace circular functions by hyperbolic ones (imaginary-radius substitution a -> ia), which sends the sphere's identities to the hyperbolic plane's.

validity_conditions: Substituting a -> ia, b -> ib, c -> ic uses cos(ix)=cosh x and sin(ix)=i sinh x, carrying the spherical identity to the hyperbolic one.
The factor i^2 = -1 in the sin-sin term flips its sign, giving the minus in the hyperbolic law.
This reflects passing from constant curvature +1 to constant curvature -1.
proof_plan:
Start from the [[Spherical Law of Cosines]]:
:$\cos c = \cos a \cos b + \sin a \sin b \cos C$
Substitute $a \mapsto i a$, $b \mapsto i b$, $c \mapsto i c$, corresponding to curvature $+1 \mapsto -1$.

From [[Cosine of Imaginary Number]] and [[Sine of Imaginary Number]]:
:$\map \cos {i x} = \cosh x, \quad \map \sin {i x} = i \sinh x$
